courses.description: Students will discuss perspectives on strategic communication and national security, while discussing and practicing public speaking skills and developing proficiency in three genres of security-related briefings. Students will work with the technical, scientific, and/or specialized data, vocabularies, processes, and products of the academic disciplines and/or fields of expertise relevant to national and international security careers.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad III
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Financing Terror and Hate
courses.description: This course will discuss terrorist financial activities, initiatives focused on countering those financial activities, and sanctions policy. This course approaches these topics through various techniques including, structured analytic tools, such as weighted ranking methods, scenario trees, causal flow diagramming, hypothesis testing, utility analysis, as well as game theory and logic will be incorporated into the course to provide students a better framework to form analytic judgments. At the end of the course, students will have gained a solid foundational understanding of the financing and counter-financing of terrorists.

courses.name: Far-Right Extremism: Violent Ideologies and Actions
courses.description: Introduces students to the ideologies, organizing patterns, and actions within far-right extremism. This will include a focus on movements within white supremacism, anti-government extremism, male supremacy, homophobia, and anti-immigrant extremism. Using as examples specific violent extremists and groups on the far-right, we will study key theories explaining extremist radicalization, recruitment, engagement, and mobilization.

courses.name: Terrorist Hostage Taking
courses.description: Examines different forms of hostage taking, drawing on theory and research from across a range of different fields, including international relations, political science, criminology, psychology, sociology and economics. We will consider these events in terms of how they are similar, how they differ and what they are designed to achieve. This course provides insights into the complicated nature of terrorism via hostage taking in order to broaden student understanding of current events. This course also gives students practical experience in finding and coding data, and studying complex human behaviors.

courses.name: Analyzing Terrorism: Simulations, Wargaming, and Strategies of Security
courses.description: Introduces students to novel, applied methods to study terrorism and security, including simulations, wargaming exercises, and red teaming. This course assumes no prior experience with these methods. Throughout the course, students will complete activities to understand the behavior of militant groups and develop security strategies to counter violent non-state actors.

courses.name: Political Assassinations
courses.description: Course topics include political assassinations, their consequences, and the possible means for their prevention, from profiling assassins to protection of potential targets. Research on political assassinations has developed from many different disciplines and so we will be drawing on theory and research from across a range of different fields, including international relations, political science, criminology, psychology, sociology and economics. In each lecture we will review the scholarly issues associated with political assassinations as well as considering the practical, counter attack challenges faced by security and law enforcement.

courses.name: Violent Non-State Actors in Latin America: Terrorism, Cartels, and Crime
courses.description: Examines why non-state actors resort to violence and crime, what tactics and strategies they use, how they fund their existence, and what can be done to counter them. Throughout the course, students will be introduced to many different types of violent non-state actors, including terrorist organizations and criminal organizations. This will all be done in the context of Latin America and students will gain an in-depth understanding of the problems that plague individual countries, as well as which issues afflict the region as a whole.

courses.name: Al-Qaeda, the Islamic State, and Global Jihadist Movements
courses.description: Provides an in-depth overview into global jihadist movements, with specific focus on the terrorist groups known as al-Qaeda and the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant. In an effort for students to come to a common understanding of key terms that will be discussed throughout the course, a session will be devoted to understanding key concepts and terms related to Islamic history. The course will also examine the Islamic State's connection and ultimate divorce from al-Qaeda. The course will all examine group finances, as well as the rise of affiliates. The course will also explore the use of foreign fighters and social media, as well as global responses to these movements and groups.

courses.name: Applying Theory to the Practice of Countering Terrorism
courses.description: Focuses on current events related to terrorism and counterterrorism, as they are discussed in mass media, and the implications of those current events on the ethical and professional conduct of the counterterrorism community. Through a discussion-based seminar, students will bring current, terrorism-related events to classroom discussion, where they will consider the media-framed current events in relation to academic research. Students will be continually challenged to draw connections between terrorism-related events in the news and relevant academic research. Furthermore, this class will use vignettes based in current events to present students with real-world ethical dilemmas that those in the professional counterterrorism community and broader national security community have to confront.
courses.prerequisite: BSST200.
courses.restriction: Restricted to students enrolled in the Global Terrorism Studies Minor (#BS07) who have earned 90 credits.
courses.additional_information: It is recommended that this course be taken in the final semester in the minor program.

courses.name: Experiential Learning in Terrorism Studies
courses.description: This course will supplement student's experiential learning experience, or internship in the field of terrorism studies and homeland security with guided reflection on their experiences.

courses.name: Internship in Terrorism Studies
courses.description: Supplements student's experiential learning experience, or internship in the field of terrorism studies and homeland security, with guided reflection on their experiences.

courses.name: Individual Study in Terrorism Studies II
courses.description: An independent study course for START Students.

courses.name: Individual Study in Terrorism Studies
courses.description: An independent study course for students in the Global Terrorism Minor program.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad IV
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Introduction to Criminal Justice
courses.description: Introduction to the administration of criminal justice in a democratic society, with emphasis on the theoretical and historical development of law enforcement. The principles of organization and administration for law enforcement; functions and specific activities; planning and research; public relations; personnel and training; inspection and control; direction; policy formulation.

courses.name: Introduction to Criminology
courses.description: Criminal behavior and the methods of its study; causation; typologies of criminal acts and offenders; punishment, correction and incapacitation; prevention of crime.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad I
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Topics in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Contemporary and emerging crimes and the response to them by criminal justice agencies. Emphasis is on the emergence of new forms of crimes or criminals.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 or CCJS105.

courses.name: Statistics for Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Introduction to descriptive and inferential statistics, graphical techniques, and the computer analysis of criminology and criminal justice data. Basic procedures of hypothesis testing, correlation and regression analysis, and the analysis of continuous and binary dependent variables. Emphasis upon the examination of research problems and issues in criminology and criminal justice.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 or CCJS105; and 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (STAT100, MATH107, MATH111, MATH120, MATH130, MATH135, MATH140).
courses.restriction: Must be in Criminology and Criminal Justice program; or permission of BSOS-Criminology & Criminal Justice department.

courses.name: Responses to Violence
courses.description: What are the dimensions of violence in the United States and worldwide, and how has humanity responded to violence? Conflict is unfortunately resolved through violence in a number of settings. It ranges from interpersonal to international in its scope. This course investigates the strengths and weaknesses of a number of resolutions to reducing violence over the course of history using both state centered and informal control.

courses.name: Criminal Law in Action
courses.description: Law as one of the methods of social control. Criminal law: its nature, sources and types; theories and historical developments. Behavioral and legal aspects of criminal acts. Classification and analysis of selected criminal offenses.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.

courses.name: Law of Criminal Investigation
courses.description: General principles and theories of criminal procedure. Due process. Arrest, search and seizure. Recent developments. Study and evaluation of evidence and proof.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS230.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad II
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Special Topics in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Topics of special interest to undergraduates in criminology and criminal justice. Offered in response to student request and faculty interest. May be delivered online.

courses.name: Special Topics in Law and Justice
courses.description: An analysis of recent developments in criminal law and their implications for criminal justice systems and research. Focus will be on Supreme Court decisions and legislative initiatives.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS105 and CCJS230.

courses.name: Criminological and Criminal Justice Research Methods
courses.description: Introduction to the formulation of research questions covering crime and justice, research designs, data collection, and interpretation and reporting in criminological and justice-system settings.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 or CCJS105; and (BIOM301, BMGT230, CCJS200, ECON230, EDMS451, GEOG306, GEOL351, GVPT422, INST314, JOUR405, PSYC200, QMMS251, QMMS451, STAT400, or SOCY201).

courses.name: Fundamentals in Criminal Justice
courses.description: Provides an overview of the three major components of the American criminal justice system: police, courts, and corrections. Each component will be explored in its development over time as well as various issues surrounding each component. This course will also cover important issues that are relevant to current debates including race, reentry, technology and crime, juvenile justice, and future directions for criminal justice.
courses.restriction: Must be enrolled at The Universities at Shady Grove; and must be in the Criminal Justice minor; or by permission of department; and must not be in the Criminology and Criminal Justice major.

courses.name: Criminal Investigations
courses.description: An introduction to modern methods used in detection, investigation, and solution of crime. Students will be taught basic and advanced investigative techniques utilized by law enforcement agencies. Analysis of actual cases will be used to demonstrate practical uses of these techniques.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS230.

courses.name: Ethics in Criminal Justice
courses.description: Introduces the study of ethics and ethical decision making as it is applied to the criminal justice system. Students will be introduced to consequential philosophers and their work, and will discuss those theories in terms of how decision making is applied in policing, courts, corrections, the juvenile system, victim services, and the medical system. There will be a special discussion of how ethical decision making intersects with racism, classism, and sexism in criminal justice. Students will be able to assess the intersections of race, gender, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, and class and the way those identities impact ethical decision making of acts.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.

courses.name: Special Topics in Criminology & Criminal Justice
courses.description: Special topics in various aspects of the field of criminology and criminal justice will be covered.

courses.name: Introduction to Criminalistics
courses.description: An introduction to modern methods used in the detection, investigation and solution of crimes. Practical analysis of evidence in a crime laboratory, including fingerprints and other impressions, firearms ID and ballistics, hairs and fibers, document examination, and use of polygraph.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS230.

courses.name: Computer and Digital Forensics
courses.description: An introduction to the methods used in the seizure and forensic analysis of computers, cell phones, and other digital evidence. Students will be familiarized with the use of digital evidence in criminal investigations, relevant case law in computer crime and digital evidence, and the challenges faced by law enforcement. Students will be introduced to the computer forensic tools used by today's law enforcement agencies and basic computer/data storage concepts. This course will include some basic practical application of these tools and concepts in a computer lab environment.

courses.name: Slavery in the Twenty First Century: Combating Human Trafficking
courses.description: What is human trafficking and how do we stop it? An introduction to the trafficking of human beings in its historical, legal, economic, political and social contexts. Scope of the global problem, different forms of human trafficking, and regional trends and practices. Roles of government, the international community and individual actors. Strategies to combat trafficking.

courses.name: Contemporary Criminological Issues
courses.description: Topics may include career criminals, prison overcrowding, prediction, ecological studies of crimes, family and delinquency, entrepreneurship in criminal justice and criminology, and similar criminological problems.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS105.

courses.name: Contemporary Legal Policy Issues
courses.description: In-depth examination of selected topics. Criminal responsibility. Socio-legal policy alternatives with regard to deviance. Law enforcement procedures for civil law and similar legal problems. Admissibility of evidence. Representation. Indigent's right to counsel.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS230.

courses.name: Major Transitions: From Undergraduate to Professional
courses.description: This course is designed to assist criminology and criminal justice students explore career opportunities. Topics will include: graduate school, law school, career opportunities in federal, state, local, and public agencies, resume writing, and internships.
courses.restriction: Must be in Criminology and Criminal Justice program; and sophomore standing or higher.

courses.name: Navigating Your Future: Transforming Your Degree into your Career
courses.description: Assists Criminology and Criminal Justice students in exploring and preparing for entering graduate school and/or the professional work world. Academic success and professional development in the criminal justice field will be emphasized. Specific topics covered in the course include graduate school options, the benefits of a social science degree, and careers in private industry, nonprofit organizations, and federal, state, and local agencies. Will also focus on job preparation skills including writing a resume, creating a cover letter, and preparing for an interview.
courses.restriction: Must be in the Criminology and Criminal Justice major (22091 and 2209L); or must be in the and Criminal Justice minor (#BS14) with 30 or more credits.

courses.name: Policing
courses.description: Critical issues relating to policing. Topics include police discretion, role of police, use of force, misconduct, police research, administration, personnel, and etc.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.

courses.name: Corrections
courses.description: Examination of the American correctional system. Identification of historical and contemporary themes, issues, and trends. Evaluation of correctional policies, practices and research.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the BSOS-Criminology & Criminal Justice department.

courses.name: Courts and Sentencing
courses.description: Contemporary issues in the American court system such as prosecution, sentencing and punishment. Theoretical perspectives on courtroom decision-making integrated with empirical research. Courts and sentencing processes, including initial charging, pretrial detention and final sentencing outcomes. Innovations in courts and sentencing.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the BSOS-Criminology & Criminal Justice department.

courses.name: Domestic Violence
courses.description: A thorough and critical examination of family violence. Topics include the historical background to family violence, methods of studying this serious issue, elder abuse, child abuse, the cultural factors involved in intimate partner violence, violence in same-sex relationships, and the criminal justice response to family violence. Although the course focuses on the American family, illustrations from other cultures are provided.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.

courses.name: Drugs and Crime
courses.description: An analysis of the role of criminal justice in the control of drug use and abuse.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad III
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Field Training in Criminology and Corrections
courses.description: Supervised field training in public or private social agencies. Group meetings, individual conferences and written program reports.
courses.restriction: Permission of BSOS-Criminology & Criminal Justice department.

courses.name: Victimology
courses.description: Overview of the history and theory of victimology. Analysis of victimization patterns with special emphasis on types of victims and crimes. The interaction between victims of crime and the criminal justice system with respect to the role of the victim and the services offered to the victim.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS105.

courses.name: Race, Crime and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Role and treatment of racial/ethnic minorities in the criminal justice system. Course will provide students with historical and theoretical framework for understanding this dynamic.

courses.name: Experiential Learning
courses.restriction: Permission of BSOS-Criminology & Criminal Justice department; and junior standing or higher.

courses.name: Independent Reading Course in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Designed for the needs of honor students in criminology and criminal justice.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS105.
courses.restriction: Must be in the Honors program.

courses.name: Independent Research in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Independent Research for CCJS Departmental Honors students.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS105.
courses.restriction: Must be in CCJS Honors Program.

courses.name: Law Enforcement Field Training
courses.description: Supervised, structured and focused field training in law enforcement agencies.
courses.restriction: Permission of BSOS-Criminology & Criminal Justice department.

courses.name: Independent Study in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Integrated reading or research under direction and supervision of a faculty member.
courses.restriction: Permission of BSOS-Criminology & Criminal Justice department.

courses.name: Gangs
courses.description: Provides students with a historical and contemporary examination of street and institutional gangs. We will address the nature and definition of gangs, types of gangs, and diversity of membership of gangs, theoretical explanations, and criminal and deviant behavior. In addition, we will analyze law enforcement responses, intervention and prevention strategies, and public policy issues.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS105.

courses.name: Seminar in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Selected topics of interest in the field of Criminology and Criminal Justice will be covered.

courses.name: Special Topics in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Topics in various aspects of the field of criminology and criminal justice will be covered.

courses.name: Security Administration
courses.description: Designed to introduce students to the complex issues of Security Administration and the critical terrorism issues facing the nation. Emphasis is placed on understanding the historical and contemporary issues effecting U.S. Counterterrorism Policy. It also explores the challenges facing today's security administrators including: ethics, classified information, intelligence, terrorist organizations and incidents, physical and personnel security, transportation and border security issues.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS340.

courses.name: Advanced Law Enforcement Administration
courses.description: The structuring of manpower, material, and systems to accomplish the major goals of social control. Personnel and systems management. Political controls and limitations on authority and jurisdiction.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS340.

courses.name: Advanced Juvenile Delinquency
courses.description: Examination of juvenile delinquency in the United States. Nature and extent of juvenile delinquency, historical approaches, sociological and criminological theories and research, social contexts including the institutions of families, schools, and peers, and social responses. Prevention, punishment, and treatment programs, both within and outside of the juvenile justice and criminal justice systems.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS105 and CCJS300.

courses.name: Crime and Delinquency Prevention
courses.description: Methods and programs in prevention of crime and delinquency.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS105 and CCJS300.

courses.name: White Collar and Organized Crime
courses.description: Definition, detection, prosecution, sentencing and impact of white collar and organized crime. Special consideration given to the role of federal law and enforcement practices.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS300; and (CCJS350 or CCJS105).

courses.name: Contemporary Criminological Theory
courses.description: Examination of the main theoretical accounts that explain the underlying causes of criminal behaviors. Explore how individual choices, socialization experiences, biological factors and social structure affect criminal behaviors.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS300 and CCJS105.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad IV
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Victim Advocacy
courses.description: Introduces the practice of victim advocacy as a profession. Students will develop an understanding of the impact of crime on the victim, and how crime impacts the path of the victim through the criminal justice and other administrative processes. A special emphasis of the course will be on introducing the students to different contexts of victim advocacy, e.g. system-based, campus-based, military-based, and community-based, as well as special topics impacting the profession of victim advocacy, e.g. grief, death notification, child protection, violence intervention, and trauma therapy. Students will also develop an understanding about how race, gender, age, sexual orientation, and ethnicity impact the way in which victims are offered and receive advocacy in different systems.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100.

courses.name: Psychology of Criminal Behavior
courses.description: Biological, environmental, and personality factors which influence criminal behaviors. Biophysiology and crime, stress and crime, maladjustment patterns, psychoses, personality disorders, aggression and violent crime, sex-motivated crime and sexual deviations, alcohol and drug abuse, and criminal behavior.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS105 and CCJS300.

courses.name: Honors Thesis Research
courses.description: Designed for students completing their honors thesis.
courses.prerequisite: CCJS100 and CCJS105.
courses.restriction: Limited to CCJS Departmental Honors students.

courses.name: Selected Topics in Criminology and Criminal Justice
courses.description: Topics of special interest to advanced undergraduates in criminology and criminal justice. Offered in response to student request and faculty interest.

courses.name: Exploring ChBE
courses.description: Overview of the specializations and career paths available in chemical and biomolecular engineering. Academic planning, policies and resources will be covered including introduction to undergraduate research, study abroad, internship and co-op opportunities as well as chemical engineering student groups. A peer mentoring program will enable students to interact with successful upper-class chemical engineering students and build their chemical engineering peer network.
courses.prerequisite: Permission of instructor; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Introduction to Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to methods of chemical engineering calculations and analysis. Stoichiometric relations, material and energy balances, and behavior of gases, vapors, liquids and solids. Analytical and computer methods.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM135; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department.
courses.restriction: Must be in Engineering: Chemical program; or permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Coffee BEANS: Brewing Engineering and Analysis for Nurturing Sustainability
courses.description: In this interdisciplinary course, students will explore the intricate journey of making one of the world's most-consumed beverage through the combined lens of sustainability and engineering. We will address the critical question: How sustainable is a daily cup of coffee? The course will begin with an overview of coffee production, from cultivation to consumption, examining energy targets, water usage, waste practices, and the environmental impact of coffee farming. Instruction in lectures will provide background on engineering concepts and types of sustainable practices. Students will engage in experiments, focusing on extraction techniques, to visualize scientific principles. The course will also align discussions with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, emphasizing the global implications of coffee production and consumption.

courses.name: Computer Methods in Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Algorithm development and application of software to the analysis of chemical engineering problems. File management and editing, graphics and numerical methods. Use of spreadsheets, statistics/math software and process simulators for the design of chemical process equipment.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE101; and must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in MATH241.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Thermodynamics I
courses.description: Principles of thermodynamics and their application to engineering problems. First and second laws of thermodynamics, properties of gases, liquids and solids, phase equilibrium, flow and non-flow systems, energy conversion, production of work from heat, thermodynamic analysis of processes, equilibrium stage operations and the thermodynamics of chemically reacting systems.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE101; and must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in CHBE250 and MATH241.
courses.restriction: Must be in Engineering: Chemical program; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Thermodynamics II
courses.description: Contemporary trends in chemical engineering thermodynamics that bridge the gap between fundamentals and applications. Thermodynamic analysis of non-ideal and structured systems; such as complex fluids, strongly fluctuating and nanoscale systems, dissipative systems, biosystems, and systems under extreme conditions.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE301.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical Engineering Seminar
courses.description: To develop oral communication skills through a series of class presentations of current chemical engineering topics.
courses.restriction: Junior standing; and must be in a major within ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Teaching Experiences in Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Students will obtain pedagogical experience by assisting with the teaching of undergraduate courses in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Undergraduate Honors Seminar
courses.description: Students will attend and write summaries of departmental seminars, along with professional development activities
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and Must be in the Chemical Engineering Honors Program.

courses.name: Statistics and Design of Experiments
courses.description: An introduction to probability, statistics, and design of experiments for chemical engineers.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHBE250, MATH241, and MATH246.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Transport Phenomena I
courses.description: Principals of fluid dynamics as applied to model development and process design. Mass, momentum and energy conservation. Statics and surface tension. Equation of Continuity and Navier-Stokes Equation with application to laminar flow. Dimensional analysis. Macroscopic balances, Bernoulli Equation and friction factors with application to turbulent flow.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHBE101, CHBE250, MATH241, and MATH246.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Transport Phenomena II
courses.description: Principles of mass and heat transfer as applied to model development and process design. Species continuity equation with application to diffusion, and convection in laminar flow. Macroscopic balances and mass transfer coefficients with application to turbulent flow. Microscopic equation of energy with application to heat conduction, and convection in laminar flow. Macroscopic energy balance and heat transfer coefficients with application to turbulent flow. Heat exchanger design.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE422.
courses.restriction: Must be in Engineering: Chemical program; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical and Biomolecular Separation Processes
courses.description: Separation by stages operations. Rate dependent separation processes. Design application in distillation, gas absorption, liquid extraction, drying, adsorption and ion exhange.
courses.restriction: Must be in Engineering: Chemical program; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Application of chemical engineering process and unit operation principals in small-scale semi-commercial equipment. Data from experimental observations are used to evaluate performance and efficiency of operations. Emphasis on correct presentation of results inreport form.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE424, CHBE426, and CHBE440.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical Kinetics and Reactor Design
courses.description: Fundamentals of chemical reaction kinetics and their application to the design and operation of chemical reactors. Reaction rate theory, homogeneous reactions and catalysis electrochemical reactions. Catalytic reactor design.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHBE301, MATH241, and MATH246.
courses.restriction: Must be in Engineering: Chemical program; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Chemical and Biomolecular Systems Analysis
courses.description: Dynamic response applied to process systems. Goals and modes of control, Laplace transformations, analysis and synthesis of simple control systems, closed loop response, dynamic testing.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE424 and CHBE426.

courses.name: Process Engineering Economics and Design I
courses.description: Principles of chemical engineering economics and process design. Equipment sizing and costing. Economic evaluation of projects. Flowsheet synthesis. Introduction to flowsheet simulators and concepts of flowsheet optimization. Synthesis of Heat Exchanger Networks and Distillation Sequences.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE424, CHBE426, and CHBE440.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Process Engineering Economics and Design II
courses.description: Application of chemical engineering principles for the design of chemical processing equipment. Representative problems in the design of chemical plants will be the focus of this capstone design class. Comprehensive reports are required.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE442 and CHBE444.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Photovoltaics: Solar Energy
courses.description: The emphasis of the class is on developing a conceptual understanding of the device physics and manufacturing processes of crystalline and thin-film photovoltaic cells, and to develop elementary computational skills necessary to quantify solar cell efficiency. The class material includes detailed, system-level energy balances necessary to understand how solar energy fits into the complete energy generation, conversion, and storage picture. Quantitative comparisons of PV technology to solar chemical conversion processes and biofuels are made.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Introduction of Machine Learning in Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Introduction of data science and machine learning approaches to modern problems in chemical engineering and materials science. This course develops data science approaches, including their foundational mathematical and statistical basis, and applies these methods to data sets of limited size and precision. Methods for regression and clustering will be developed and applied, with an emphasis on validation and error quantification. Techniques that will be developed include linear and nonlinear regression, clustering and logistic regression, dimensionality reduction, unsupervised learning, and artificial neural networks. These methods will be applied to a range of engineering problems, including conducting polymers, stretchable conductors, organic synthesis, and quality control in manufacturing.
courses.recommended: Basic knowledge of chemical engineering, materials science, ordinary differential equations, and Python is desirable.
courses.restriction: Permission of Department or Instructor.

courses.name: Chemical Process Analysis and Optimization
courses.description: Application of mathematical models to the analysis and optimization of chemical processes. Models based on transport, chemical kinetics and other chemical engineering principles will be employed.

courses.name: Model Predictive Control
courses.description: Empirical model identification from process data. Step and impulse response models. Linearization of nonlinear first principles models. Single variable Model Predictive Control. Robustness with respect to modeling error. MPC based tuning of PID controllers. Feedforward control. Multi-input multi-output processes. Multi-loop decentralized control. Centralized multivariable Model Predictive Control via on-line optimization.

courses.name: Applications of Materials in Biology and Medicine
courses.description: Provides a foundation for understanding the use of various materials in medical applications. We will discuss design principles, based on biological context for drug delivery, diagnosis of disease, imaging applications, tissue engineering, among other relevant topics. The course will cover nanomedicine approaches (lipids, polymers, gold nanoparticles, carbon nanotubes, etc.), as well as scaffolds for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. We will discuss advantages, challenges, and recent advances in the field. The course will highlight the importance of rational engineering when designing products to be used to treat and diagnose disease.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in MATH246; and CHEM231; and (CHBE301, ENMA461, or BIOE232).
courses.recommended: Knowledge of basic fluid dynamics: CHBE422/BIOE331 or equivalent.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Research
courses.description: Investigation of a research project under the direction of a faculty member. Comprehensive reports are required.
courses.restriction: Permission of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Department; and must be third or fourth year student; and must have minimum GPA of 3.0; and must have successfully completed all lower level engineering, science and mathematics courses for the major.

courses.name: Special Projects
courses.description: Special project under the direction of a faculty member. Comprehensive reports are required.
courses.restriction: Permission of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Department; and must be third or fourth year student; and must have minimum GPA of 3.0; and must have successfully completed all lower level engineering, science and mathematics courses for the major.

courses.name: Colloid and Interface Science
courses.description: Introduction to colloidal systems and interfacial science. Topics include preparation, stability and coagulation kinetics of colloidal suspensions. Introduction to DLVO theory, electrokinetic phenomena, colloidal aggregation, interfacial phenomena, double layer theory, surface chemistry. Discussion of interfacial thermodynamics and interfacial forces for solid-liquid interfaces. Applications to nanomaterial synthesis, nanomaterial and polymer self-assembly, protein-protein interactions, and protein aggregation will be discussed.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE424 and CHBE426.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Particle Science and Technology
courses.description: Particles are everywhere. We breathe them, eat them, and use them to make many non-particulate materials. Knowledge of particle science and technology is important for manufacturing, for occupational health and safety, as well as environmental considerations. In this multidisciplinary course, the focus will be on the study of science and technology relevant to multiphase systems consisting of solid and/or liquid particles surrounded by a gas. These topics fall loosely under the headings of powder and aerosol technology. Team design projects will be an integral component.
courses.prerequisite: Knowledge of undergraduate engineering thermodynamics, and transport phenomena; knowledge of numerical methods for solving systems of ordinary differential equations.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; or permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Control of Air Pollution Sources
courses.description: Sources and effects of air pollutants, regulatory trends, atmospheric dispersion models, fundamentals of two-phase flow as applied to air pollution and air pollution control systems, design of systems for control of gases and particulate matter.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Advanced Batteries and Fuel Cells
courses.description: The lecture will start from the basic electrochemical thermodynamics and kinetics, with emphasis on electrochemical techniques, fundamental principle and performance of batteries, and supercapacitors.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Biopharmaceutical Process Development and Manufacturing
courses.description: Covers the fundamental steps involved in process development and manufacturing of biopharmaceuticals. An overview of different classes of biopharmaceuticals as well as manufacturing requirements for clinical development and regulatory approval will be provided. In depth coverage of manufacturing steps including cell culture, purification and formulation as well as drug product manufacturing, analysis and stability will be covered. Scientific literature will be used to highlight current challenges and novel solutions in each step of the manufacturing process. Scale up considerations, GMP requirements and process economics will also be introduced.
courses.prerequisite: BIOE120; and permission of instructor.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Ethics in Science and Engineering
courses.description: Ethical issues in science and engineering and their resolutions are examined. The main topics will be ethics and scientific truth (including issues of proper data analysis, proper data presentation, and record-keeping), ethics and other scientists and engineers (including issues of attribution, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, mentoring, and inclusion of under-represented groups), ethics and the practice of engineering (including responsibilities of engineers to clients, ecological issues, and conflicts of interest), and ethics and society (including funding priorities, moral issues, and human and animal subjects). Class meetings will be organized around discussions, case studies, and student reports. The course is aimed at postdoctoral students, graduate students and advanced undergraduate students who wish to ponder the important contemporary questions about the ethics of how science and engineering get done.

courses.name: Molecular Modeling Methods
courses.description: Statistical mechanics will be introduced to give the fundamental background for atomic to mesoscale molecular modeling. Classical atomic-level simulations methods (Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics) and the procedures to develop intra- and intermolecular potentials will be covered. This course will also discuss the theory and application of coarse-grained molecular simulations, mesoscale simulations and other modern simulation techniques. A broad range of applications will be included throughout the semester, e.g., phase behavior of small molecules, kinetics, and biophysics.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Mesoscopic and Nanoscale Thermodynamics
courses.description: Interdisciplinary course primarily for graduate and senior undergraduate students from engineering or science departments. New emerging technologies deal with bio-membrane and gene engineering, microreactor chemistry and microcapsule drug delivery, micro-fluids and porous media, nanoparticles and nanostructures, supercritical fluid extraction and artifical organs. Engineers often design processes where classical thermodynamics may be insufficient, e.g., strongly fluctuating and nanoscale systems, or dissipative systems under conditions far away from equilibrium.
courses.prerequisite: A prior course in classical thermodynamics.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Bionanotechnology: Physical Principles
courses.description: Physics at nano/micro scales. Biomolecular building blocks. Simplest biomolecular assembly: protein folding. Nanoscale intermolecular interactions important for biology. Protein-ligand binding. Protein higher-order assembly: filaments, networks. Protein filaments and motility. DNA, RNA and their assembly assisted by proteins. Viral capsid assembly. Lipid assembly into micelles, bilayers. Lipid-protein co-assembly in membranes. Lipid and polymer structures useful in medicine. Targeted delivery of drugs, genes by nano/micro structures. Cellular assembly in the eye, in insect wings. Cellular assembly at surfaces: gecko feet, duck feathers. Cellular assembly in the presence of crystals: biomineralization.
courses.prerequisite: BIOE120; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Transport Phenomena in Small and Biological Systems
courses.description: Interdisciplinary course primarily for senior undergraduate and graduate students from engineering or science departments. The course's main goal is to make the students familiar with the fundamental physics and modeling of transport phenomena in small and biological systems, and their current scientific and engineering utilization in microfluidics, nanofluidics and biological systems.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.
courses.additional_information: Adding graduate course to jointly offered and credit only granted for fields.

courses.name: Bioseparations
courses.description: Engineering fundamentals of separations and purification of biological molecules. Case studies and examples illustrate principles and practice of centrifugation, precipitation, crystallization, filtration, membrane separations, chromatography, and affinity separation of recombinant proteins and other biomolecules. Process scale-up and economics of biotechnology products and processes.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Metabolic Pathway Engineering
courses.description: The state-of-the-art in metabolic engineering, with a focus on the analysis and engineering of metabolic pathways through (chemical) engineering principles, will be covered. Topics covered include: (1) overview of biochemistry and metabolism; (2) metabolic flux analysis and isotope labeling illustrated with examples from the recent scientific literature; (3) technologies for engineering metabolic pathways; (4) metabolic control analysis and pathway regulation; (5) applications of metabolic engineering to synthesis of biofuels and therapeutics; (6) specialized and related subjects such as protein engineering and synthetic biology.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE101 and CHBE440.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Biochemical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Techniques of measuring pertinent parameters in fermentation reactors, quantification of production variables for primary and secondary metabolites such as enzymes and antibiotics, the insolubilization of enzymes for reactors, and the demonstration of separation techniques such as ultrafiltration and affinity chromatography.

courses.name: Heterogeneous Catalysis for Energy Applications
courses.description: Introduction to heterogeneous catalytic science and technology for energy conversion and hydocarbon processing. Preparation and mechanistic characterization of catalyst systems, kinetics of catalyzed reactions, adsorption and diffusion influences in heterogenious reactions. An overview of heterogeneous catalysis in various energy-related applications, including petroleum refining, chemicals from biomass, valorization of shale gas, and CO2 utilization will be introduced.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHBE302, CHBE424, and CHBE440; and permission of instructor.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Polymer Science
courses.description: The elements of the polymer chemistry and industrial polymerization, polymer structures and physics, thermodynamics of polymer solutions, polymer processing methods, and engineering applications of polymers.

courses.name: Electrochemical Energy Engineering
courses.description: Introduces students to the fundamentals of electrochemical engineering, covering thermodynamics, kinetics, and transport in electrochemical cells, as well as electrode structures and electroanalytical techniques. The course will next transition to focus on electrochemical devices, including batteries, fuel cells, and other devices as guided by student input. This course will serve as a foundation for students who are interested in becoming practicing electrochemical engineers, those who would like to pursue research careers, and those who wish to become familiar with a specialized area within engineering that will have a crucial and growing importance during their careers.
courses.prerequisite: CHBE302, CHBE440, and CHBE422.
courses.restriction: Permission of ENGR - Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering Department.

courses.name: Chemical Processes in Beer Brewing
courses.description: Covers chemical engineering principles and chemical processes involved in the brewing and quality control of beer. Topics will include extraction and isomerization of bittering compounds from hops, enzymatic reactions involved in mashing beer, colloidal chemistry of haze formation, and microbiology of yeast and fermentation. Quantitative models will be applied to these processes based on fundamental chemical engineering principles from reaction kinetics, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, and colloid and interfacial science.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHBE424 and CHBE440; and permission of instructor.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and permission of ENGR- & Biomolecular Engineering department.
courses.additional_information: Neither the students nor the instructor will be making or working with alcoholic beverages in the course.

courses.name: Sustainable Separations and Carbon Capture
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of sustainable separations and carbon dioxide capture using synthetic membranes and sorbents.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHBE424, CHBE426 and CHBE440; and permission of instructor.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within the ENGR-Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering department; and must have permission of ENGR- & Biomolecular Engineering department.

courses.name: Polymeric Materials: Structure, Property, and Processing
courses.description: An intermediate level treatment of structures of polymers. An introduction to mechanical properties and processing of polymeric materials. Emphasis will be on how to establish the structure-property relationship and on how to achieve such understanding via different characterization methods.
courses.prerequisite: ENMA300; and permission of ENGR-Materials Science & Engineering department.

courses.name: Protein Engineering
courses.description: This course will cover the fundamentals of protein engineering and its applications in medicine, chemical processes, and energy. Topics will include the structure and function of biological molecules, rational design and directed evolution, construction of protein and peptide libraries, protein screening platforms, methods for characterizing structure and function of biological molecules. Scientific literature will be used to highlight key discoveries and current work in protein engineering.
courses.prerequisite: BIOE120, CHBE302, and CHBE440; and permission of instructor.

courses.name: Chemistry I - Fundamentals of General Chemistry
courses.description: An overview of the Periodic Table, inorganic substances, ionic and covalent bonding, bulk properties of materials, chemical equilibrium, and quantitative chemistry. CHEM131 is the first course in a four-semester sequence for students majoring in the sciences, other than Chemistry and Biochemistry majors.
courses.prerequisite: Must have math eligibility of MATH120 or higher.
courses.credit_only_granted_for: CHEM103, CHEM131, CHEM135, CHEM153 or CHEM146.

courses.name: General Chemistry I Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to the quantification of chemical substances, including the concept of the mole and chemical stoichiometry. Additional work involves the synthesis of ionic substances and their qualitative characterization. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM131.
courses.prerequisite: Must have math eligibility of MATH120 or higher.
courses.credit_only_granted_for: CHEM103, CHEM132, CHEM136, CHEM143, CHEM147 or CHEM177.

courses.name: Chemical Principles for Engineering
courses.description: Basic chemistry for engineering students. Introduction to organic structures and polymers, gas laws, liquids, solids, phase changes, chemical kinetics and electrochemistry.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHEM131; or minimum grade of C- in CHEM146.

courses.name: General Chemistry for Engineers
courses.description: The nature and composition of matter, solutions, chemical reactions, equilibria, and electrochemistry, with applications to various fields of engineering.
courses.prerequisite: Must have math eligibility of MATH120 or higher.
courses.credit_only_granted_for: CHEM103, CHEM113, CHEM131, CHEM135, or CHEM146.

courses.name: General Chemistry Laboratory for Engineers
courses.description: A laboratory course for engineering majors intending to take CHEM231 and CHEM232.
courses.prerequisite: Must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in CHEM135 and must have math eligibility of MATH120 or higher.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major in ENGR-A. James Clark School of Engineering.

courses.name: Principles of General Chemistry
courses.description: An overview of the Periodic Table, inorganic substances, ionic and covalent bonding, bulk properties of materials, chemical equilibrium, and quantitative chemistry. CHEM146 is the first course in a four-semester sequence for Chemistry and Biochemistry majors.
courses.prerequisite: Must have math eligibility of MATH140 or higher.
courses.restriction: Must be in one of the following programs (Chemistry; Biochemistry).
courses.credit_only_granted_for: CHEM103, CHEM131, CHEM135, CHEM143, or CHEM146.

courses.name: Introduction to Laboratory Practices and Research in the Chemical Sciences
courses.description: First semester laboratory course required for CHEM and BCHM majors. Introduction to laboratory techniques, including safety practices, scientific ethics, and presentation of current research topics.
courses.prerequisite: Must have math eligibility of MATH120 or higher.
courses.restriction: Must be in a major within CMNS-Chemistry & Biochemistry department; or permission of CMNS-Chemistry & Biochemistry department.

courses.name: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: The chemistry of carbon: aliphatic compounds, aromatic compounds, stereochemistry, arenes, halides, alcohols, esters and spectroscopy.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM131, CHEM135, or CHEM146; and (CHEM132, CHEM136, CHEM147, or CHEM177); and a grade of C- or better in the prerequisites is required of College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences majors and recommended for all students.

courses.name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Provides experience in developing some basic laboratory techniques, recrystallization, distillation, extraction, chromatography.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM131 and CHEM132; or (CHEM135 and CHEM136); or (CHEM146 and CHEM147). And a grade of C- or better in the prerequisites is required for College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences majors and recommended for all students.

courses.name: Principles of Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: The chemistry of carbons: aliphatic compounds, aromatic compounds, stereochemistry, arenes, halides, alcohols, esters, and spectroscopy.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM131, CHEM135, or CHEM146; and (CHEM132, CHEM136, or CHEM147); and a grade of C- or better in the prerequisites is required of College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences majors and recommended for all students. Or permission of CMNS-Chemistry & Biochemistry department.
courses.restriction: Must be in one of the following programs (Chemistry; Biochemistry) ; or must be in a major in ENGR-A. James Clark School of Engineering.

courses.name: Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: A continuation of CHEM231 with emphasis on molecular structure; substitution reactions; carbonium ions; aromaticity; synthetic processes; macromolecules.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM231 and CHEM232; or CHEM237. And a grade of C- or better in the prerequisites is required for College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences majors and recommended for all students.

courses.name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: Synthetic organic chemistry through functional group manipulation, introduction to instrumentation essential to analysis and structure elucidation.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM231 and CHEM232; or CHEM237. And a grade of C- or better in the prerequisites is required for College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences majors and recommended for all students.

courses.name: Principles of Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: A continuation of CHEM237 with emphasis on molecular structure, substitution reactions; carbonium ions; aromaticity; synthetic processes; macromolecules.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHEM237; or permission of CMNS-Chemistry & Biochemistry department.
courses.restriction: Must be in one of the following programs (Chemistry; Biochemistry) ; or must be an honors student.

courses.name: General Chemistry and Energetics
courses.description: An introduction to the physical aspects of chemistry; chemical kinetics, thermodynamics and electrochemistry in the context of current chemistry research.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM241 and CHEM242; or CHEM247. And a grade of C- or better in the prerequisites for College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences majors and recommended for all students.

courses.name: General Bioanalytical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: An introduction to analytical chemistry with an emphasis on bio-analytical instrumentation and techniques.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM241 and CHEM242; or CHEM247. And a grade of C- or better in the prerequisites is required for College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences majors and recommended for all students.

courses.name: General Chemistry and Energetics - Majors
courses.description: An introduction to the physical aspects of chemistry for Biochemistry and Chemistry majors. Chemical kinetics, thermodynamics and electrochemistry in the context of current chemistry research.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHEM241 and CHEM242; or minimum grade of C- in CHEM247.
courses.restriction: Must be in one of the following programs (Chemistry; Biochemistry).

courses.name: Fundamentals of Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Quantitative analysis, inorganic analytical chemistry, and an introduction to bio-analytical instrumentation and techniques.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHEM241 and CHEM242; or minimum grade of C- in CHEM247.
courses.restriction: Must be in one of the following programs (Chemistry; Biochemistry).

courses.name: Special Topics in Chemistry
courses.description: Course topics to be determined by instructor.

courses.name: Quantum Steampunk Science-Fiction Workshop
courses.description: Steampunk is a science-fiction genre in which futuristic technologies populate Victorian-era settings. Recently, steampunk has come to life in the scientific field of quantum thermodynamics. Thermodynamics, the study of energy, grew out of the Industrial Revolution. Two centuries later, quantum physics is transforming computing and cryptography. Quantum science is now revolutionizing 19th-century thermodynamics in quantum thermodynamics, which features quantum engines, automata, and more. Quantum thermodynamics inspired the growing subgenre of quantum steampunk. In this course, you will read science fiction, write quantum steampunk short stories, receive feedback, and critique classmates' writing. In parallel, you will learn about quantum physics, technologies, and thermodynamics.
courses.credit_only_granted_for: ARHU270, ARHU298Q, CHEM298Q, CMSC298Q, ENGL289Q, ENME299Q or PHYS299Q.

courses.name: Chemical Demonstrations and Outreach
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide students with the experience, skills, and knowledge of performing chemical demonstrations. The goal is to illustrate chemical principles using engaging and visually stimulating experiments. There will be an emphasis on safety and understanding the chemistry behind how each chemical demonstration works. In addition to learning experiments, students will be expected to perform an outreach project.
courses.prerequisite: (CHEM241 and CHEM242) or CHEM247; and (CHEM271 or CHEM276) and (CHEM272 or CHEM277).
courses.restriction: Permission of the Chemistry and Biochemistry Department.

courses.name: Pedagogy and Instruction in Chemistry
courses.description: Methodologies, theory and educational tools applicable to the field of undergraduate chemistry education. Examples covered will use content from introductory general and organic chemistry courses.
courses.prerequisite: Permission of instructor; and minimum grade of B- in CHEM231; and must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in CHEM241.

courses.name: Professional Issues in Chemistry and Biochemistry
courses.description: Seminar on professional issues. Professional responsibilities, ethics, interview techniques, career opportunities, graduate/professional school, race and gender issues.
courses.restriction: Junior standing or higher; and must be in one of the following programs (Chemistry; Biochemistry).

courses.name: Special Projects
courses.description: Honors projects for undergraduate students.

courses.name: Introduction to Chemical Research
courses.description: Basic (chemical) research conducted under the supervision of a faculty member.
courses.restriction: Junior standing or higher; and permission of CMNS-Chemistry & Biochemistry department.

courses.name: Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: An overview of basic concepts of the electronic structure of the elements, chemical bonding and reactivity, from simple diatomic molecules to coordination compounds. These are viewed from simple (Lewis) to the most comprehensive molecular orbital theory. Symmetry and group theory are used throughout the course.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM276 or CHEM271; and (CHEM247 or CHEM241).

courses.name: Radiochemistry
courses.description: Radioactive decay; introduction to properties of atomic nuclei; nuclear processes in cosmology; chemical, biomedical and environmental applications of radioactivity; nuclear processes as chemical tools; interaction of radiation with matter.
courses.prerequisite: Must have completed one year of college chemistry and one year of college physics.

courses.name: Instrumental Methods of Analysis
courses.description: Modern instrumentation in analytical chemistry. Electronics, spectroscopy, chromatography and electrochemistry.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM272 and CHEM271; or (CHEM276 and CHEM277).

courses.name: Atmospheric Chemistry and Climate
courses.description: The effects of human activity on atmospheric composition, focused on global warming, the carbon cycle, air pollution, and the ozone layer. Fundamentals of atmosphereic chemistry (spectroscopy, kinetics, isotopic analysis, and biogeochemical cycles) are related to the modern understanding of climate change, air quality, and ozone depletion, based on resources such as satellite missions, field campaigns, and scientific assessments published by international agencies. We also examine how society's energy needs could be met, in the future, in a manner with less impact on atmospheric composition than the present heavy reliance on combusion of fossil fuels.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM131, CHEM135, or CHEM146. And MATH241; or permission of CMNS-Atmospheric & Oceanic Science department; or permission of CMNS-Chemistry & Biochemistry department. Cross-listed with AOSC433.

courses.name: Air Pollution and Environmental Justice
courses.description: Basic concepts in physics and chemistry of the atmosphere as applied to air pollution and environmental justice. Production, transformation, spatial scales, transport, and removal of air pollutants. The problems of photochemical smog, the greenhouse effect & climate change, stratospheric ozone, visibility. Numerical simulation of air pollution. Health and environmental effects of air pollution in the developed and developing world; why some communities suffer disproportionately
courses.prerequisite: CHEM131 and MATH241; or permission of instructor.

courses.name: Advanced Organic Chemistry
courses.description: An advanced study of the compounds of carbon, with special emphasis on molecular orbital theory and organic reaction mechanisms.
courses.prerequisite: Must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in CHEM480 or CHEM481; and 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (CHEM241, CHEM247).

courses.name: Structure Determination Using Spectroscopic Methods
courses.description: The use of infrared, ultraviolet-visible, proton and carbon-13 nuclear magnetic resonance and mass spectroscopy for structure determination in organic chemistry.
courses.prerequisite: Must have completed CHEM243; or CHEM247; or (CHEM241 and CHEM242).

courses.name: Techniques in Pulse NMR
courses.description: NMR techniques to operate, adjust, and calibrate the spectrometers and acquire and process NMR data in one and two dimensional NMR applications.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM241 and CHEM242; or CHEM247.
courses.restriction: Senior standing or higher.
courses.additional_information: Persons with heart pacemakers and/or metal implants cannot take the course due to potential health hazards.

courses.name: Principles of Physical Chemistry
courses.description: Covers elementary thermodynamics, principles of kinetics and catalysis and selected topics in molecular quantum mechanics, spectroscopy and statistical mechanics. Topics will emphasize core subjects along with applications to biosciences, materials science, environmental science and related areas.
courses.prerequisite: (CHEM276 or CHEM271); and (CHEM277 or CHEM272); and (MATH140 or MATH136); and (PHYS260 and PHYS261) or PHYS132.
courses.credit_only_granted_for: CHEM480 or CHEM481; CHEM480, BCHM485 or CHEM482.

courses.name: Physical Chemistry I
courses.description: Thermodynamics and kinetics of chemical and molecular systems. Topics may include internal energy, heat, work, enthalpy, entropy, free energy, and spontaneity as well as reaction order, differential rate laws, integrated rate laws, and rate laws for multi-step processes.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHEM135; or minimum grade of C- in CHEM271 and CHEM272; or minimum grade of C- in CHEM276 and CHEM277. And minimum grade of C- in MATH141. And minimum grade of C- in PHYS260 and PHYS261; or minimum grade of C- in PHYS142.

courses.name: Physical Chemistry II
courses.description: Quantum mechanical nature of atoms and molecules. Topics may include model systems for electronic, vibrational, rotational and translational energies as well as connections to molecular spectroscopy and thermal distributions.
courses.prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHEM135; or minimum grade of C- in CHEM271 and CHEM272; or minimum grade of C- in CHEM276 and CHEM277. And minimum grade of C- in MATH141. And minimum grade of C- in PHYS260 and PHYS261; or minimum grade of C- in PHYS142.

courses.name: Physical Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: An introduction to the principles and application of quantitative techniques in physical chemical measurements. Experiments will be coordinated with topics in CHEM481.
courses.prerequisite: Must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in CHEM481.

courses.name: Physical Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: Advanced quantitative techniques necessary in physical chemical measurements. Experiments will be coordinated with topics in CHEM 482.
courses.prerequisite: Must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in CHEM482.

courses.name: Special Topics in Chemistry
courses.prerequisite: Prerequisite varies with the nature of the topic being considered.

courses.name: Introduction to Chinese Language and Culture
courses.description: An introduction to the Chinese language and Chinese culture, covering the linguistic, ethnic, and religious diversity of China, and to explore the rich nuances of Chinese culture. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including the origins and evolution of Chinese characters, poetry, philosophy, calligraphy, and painting.

courses.name: Intensive Elementary Chinese I
courses.description: Introduction to speaking, reading, and writing Chinese with an emphasis on mastering the essentials of pronunciation, basic characters and structural patterns.
courses.prerequisite: Must have attained appropriate World Language Placement Test (WLPT) score.

courses.name: Elementary Spoken Chinese
courses.description: Continued study of grammatical patterns and vocabulary buildup with particular emphasis on conversation.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN101; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department; or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement (WLP) score.
courses.additional_information: Must be taken in conjunction with CHIN103.

courses.name: Elementary Written Chinese
courses.description: Continued study of grammatical patterns and buildup of vocabulary with particular emphasis on reading and writing.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN101; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department; or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement Test (WLPT) score.
courses.additional_information: Must be taken in conjunction with CHIN102.

courses.name: Elementary Chinese - Accelerated Track
courses.description: Accelerated instruction in Mandarin Chinese at the elementary level for students with prior Chinese language background, either through home use or formal instruction.
courses.prerequisite: Must have appropriate World Language Placement (WLP) score.
courses.restriction: Must not have completed CHIN103, CHIN102, or CHIN101.

courses.name: Elementary Chinese I
courses.description: Introduces Chinese phonetic system and writing system; develops students' Chinese proficiency on the basic linguistic skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing as well as their cultural competence.
courses.prerequisite: ACTLF Novice Low proficiency in all language skills, or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement score.

courses.name: Elementary Chinese II
courses.description: Develops students' communicative competence to ACTFL Novice Mid/High level of proficiency. Introduces students to Chinese culture.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN121; or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement score.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad I
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Intermediate Spoken Chinese I
courses.description: Emphasis on development of conversational skills with vocabulary build-up and controlled conversation.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN102; or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement (WLP) score.
courses.additional_information: Must be taken in conjunction with CHIN202.

courses.name: Intermediate Written Chinese I
courses.description: Reading and writing skills with emphasis on grammar and Chinese characters.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN103; or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement (WLP) score.
courses.additional_information: Must be taken in conjunction with CHIN201.

courses.name: Intermediate Spoken Chinese II
courses.description: Continuation of CHIN201.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN201; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department; or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement (WLP) score.
courses.additional_information: Must be taken in conjunction with CHIN204.

courses.name: Intermediate Written Chinese II
courses.description: Continuation of CHIN202.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN202; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department; or must have attained appropriate World Language Placement (WLP) score.
courses.additional_information: Must be taken in conjunction with CHIN203.

courses.name: Intermediate Chinese - Accelerated Track
courses.description: Accelerated instruction in Mandarin Chinese at the intermediate level for students with prior Chinese language background, either through home use or formal instruction.
courses.prerequisite: Must have attained appropriate World Language Placement (WLP) score.
courses.restriction: Must not have completed CHIN201, CHIN203, CHIN202, or CHIN204.

courses.name: Intermediate Chinese II
courses.description: Builds upon the foundation of CHIN206, advancing students' proficiency in both spoken and written Mandarin at the intermediate level through culturally rich, context-driven learning. Emphasizing language as a form of social interaction, the course deepens students' understanding of Chinese pragmatics--how to use Mandarin appropriately across diverse social contexts. Through a task-based, communicative approach, students engage in real-world scenarios such as course enrollment, intercultural dialogue, and campus life interactions, while exploring the cultural nuances behind everyday expressions like greetings. Role-centered activities and a language exchange program with Chinese speakers foster reflection and intercultural competence, empowering learners to navigate Chinese-speaking environments with confidence and cultural sensitivity.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN206.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad II
courses.description: Special topics course taken as part of an approved study abroad program.

courses.name: Advanced Chinese I
courses.description: Readings in expository and fictional writing with conversation and composition.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN203 and CHN204; or CHIN207; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department.

courses.name: Advanced Chinese II
courses.description: Continuation of CHIN301.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN301; or students who have taken courses with comparable content may contact the department. And must have taken a placement interview offered by the department for Non-majors.

courses.name: Life in China through TV Plays I
courses.description: Using authentic Chinese language material in short TV plays to learn about society and life in China.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN203 and CHIN204; or permission of ARHU-School of Languages, Literatures, and Cultures department.

courses.name: Life in China through TV Plays II
courses.description: Continuation of CHIN305 using authentic Chinese language material in TV plays to learn about society and life in China.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN305; or permission of ARHU-School of Languages, Literatures, and Cultures department.

courses.name: Linguistic Landscape of China
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to Chinese and other major languages in the Sino-Tibetan, Altaic, Austroasiatic, and Austronesian families, all of which are spoken in China. Taught in English.
courses.prerequisite: Must have completed CHIN204 or above; or permission of Chinese Program Advisor.

courses.name: Chinese Poetry and Prose in Translation
courses.description: Writing of the major poets, essayists, and historians from the 10th century B.C. to the 12th century A.D. No knowledge of Chinese is required.

courses.name: Modern Chinese Literature in Translation
courses.description: Major works of fiction and drama from 1920 to the present read in the context of social and literary change. Emphasis on western and traditional Chinese influences on the writers and their works. No knowledge of Chinese required.

courses.name: Chinese Calligraphy: Theory and Practice
courses.description: History of the writing system; major scripts, modes, and styles. Intermediate brushwork and lectures on the culture. Characters for practice selected to correspond to lecture topics. Taught in English.
courses.prerequisite: CHIN220; or permission of instructor.

courses.name: Chinese Culture through Traditional Chinese Arts
courses.description: Study of calligraphy, music, painting, and taichi coupled with critical readings of scholarly and literary texts. Facilitates an understanding of China and Chinese culture through traditional Chinese arts. Taught in English.

courses.name: Special Topics in Study Abroad III
